description: How a raw CXC v0.2.40 recording becomes a stored fixture, and how a Go replay's output is brought to the same form before comparison (contracts.md section 3). Applied in this order to every stdout, stderr, stub call argument, observed path and observed file text: placeholders (each bound absolute path, longest first, as given and symlink-resolved), then the text rules in order, then the aliases. Stderr first loses the lines drop_stderr_lines matches. The oracle also runs under a frozen clock (2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, +1 ms per Date reading) with TZ=UTC; the text rules still replace timestamps, because a Go replay has no frozen clock.

placeholders.is: the oracle's plugins/codexclaw directory (the host's PLUGIN_ROOT); a Go replay binds the crw plugin root
the oracle checkout root (bin/codexclaw.mjs lives here); a Go replay binds nothing, no crw text names it
the case workspace: the process cwd and the hook payload cwd
CODEXCLAW_HOME; a Go replay binds CRW_HOME here (name-substitution.json R13)
the directory of fake external programs at the head of PATH
the directory holding only node and git, the rest of PATH
the recorder's own files (fake clock, stub scripts, call log); never observed
the case root holding all of the above

text.name: plugin-version
text.why: the payload manifest version; a Go replay prints its own

text.name: iso-timestamp
text.why: updatedAt, createdAt, at, ts, injectedAt, observedAt, acquiredAt, startedAt, finishedAt and receipt times

text.name: json-compact-stamp
text.why: a 14-digit stamp stored as a JSON number stays valid JSON once replaced

text.name: compact-stamp
text.why: the 14-digit UTC stamp inside cycle and epoch nonces (orchestrate-cli.ts:97, hook.ts:120,129)

text.name: json-epoch-ms
text.why: Date.now() stored as a JSON number (state, records, SQLite rows dumped as JSON) stays valid JSON once replaced

text.name: epoch-ms
text.why: Date.now() values and names derived from them (evidence-unrecordable/<s>-<a>-<ms>.json, tmp names)

text.name: node-pid
text.why: Node prefixes its own diagnostics with the pid

text.name: json-pid
text.why: lock owner and background-job pids (state.ts:676, goalplan owner.json, bg records)

text.name: text-duration
text.why: wall-clock timings in recall's plain-text headers: '(3/4 files scanned, 1ms)', 'pruned, 2ms)'

text.name: uid-dir
text.why: the spawn grant store is per uid (spawn-attach-hook.ts:365)

text.name: manifest-digest
text.why: digests of the Node payload files; a Go build digests its own binary, so these never compare

alias.name: uuid
alias.why: randomUUID: dispatch attempt ids, temporary names

alias.name: nonce
alias.why: cycle (c-), epoch (e-) and other <prefix>-<stamp>-<3 random bytes> ids

alias.name: bg-id
alias.why: background job ids: bg + 3 random bytes (bg-wake/src/spawn.ts:28)

alias.name: spawn-nonce
alias.why: the subspawn grant nonce (32 random bytes) after GRANT: in the [CXC-SUBSPAWN-GRANT:...] marker (spawn-attach-hook.ts:378); only the nonce is aliased

alias.name: claimed-suffix
alias.why: the random suffix of a claimed grant file (spawn-attach-hook.ts:397)

alias.name: subspawn-grant-path
alias.why: the grant directory is sha256(absolute cwd, session) (spawn-attach-hook.ts:364-367), so it differs with the case root

alias.name: subspawn-grant-file
alias.why: a grant file is named sha256(random nonce) (spawn-attach-hook.ts:370-372)

alias.name: catalog-key
alias.why: model-catalog.json key = sha256 of CODEX_HOME, CODEX_MODELS_CACHE_PATH, PATH, OPENCODEX_HOME (live-catalog.ts:55-58), all case-root paths

drop_stderr_lines.name: node-warning
drop_stderr_lines.why: Node's own runtime warnings (ExperimentalWarning for node:sqlite, stripTypeScriptTypes); not CXC output

drop_stderr_lines.name: node-warning-hint
drop_stderr_lines.regex: ^\(Use `node --trace-warnings \.\.\.` to show where the warning was created\)$
drop_stderr_lines.why: the hint line Node prints after its first warning
